about: The SET-level record measures, as data: est. 1RM (Epley), the number a set is ranked by for the est.-1RM record (comparableValue), top weight (weightLb) and the pound conversion under all of them. Run by BOTH frontend/src/utils/formulas.test.js and backend/src/test/java/com/worktrac/backend/stats/SetMeasuresTest.java, so the celebration and badges (client) cannot disagree with the PRs board, records table and Trends chart (server) about the same set.

Expected values are STRINGS so each side reads them exactly: Java as BigDecimal (compared exactly), JavaScript as the nearest double (compared with ===). Both implementations compute in exact arithmetic, so there is no tolerance anywhere.
The epley ties (x.x5 before rounding) are the cases that matter: the two sides used to round them opposite ways -- 187.5 x 7 showed 231.3 in the celebration and 231.2 on the PRs board.

epley.name: a tie the old browser maths rounded DOWN
a tie at the smallest scale
a single whose weight is itself a tie
the estimate is unit-free (kg in, kg out)

toLb.name: kg converts exactly (floating point lands a hair high here)

comparableValue.name: a loaded lb set ranks on its est. 1RM
a loaded kg set ranks on its est. 1RM in pounds
a tie in kg converts after rounding
a bodyweight set ranks on its raw rep count
the rep cap does not apply at bodyweight
added load does not enter a hold's rank

weightLb.name: bodyweight is zero, so it is never a top-weight record
